question: Does retaining four forward-only temporal stages retain more validation performance than two bidirectional stages, before and after matched recovery training?

historical_evidence.scope: Historical teachers; training-free validation screening only, not the final publication teachers.

recovery.initialization: same-cell final-v1 S1 checkpoint, encoder and heads inherited
recovery.stream: exact SHA-verified existing K1 batch stream
recovery.checkpoint_selection: highest validation MacroDomainF1 after an epoch; strict improvement; earliest epoch on ties; epoch-zero screen is excluded
recovery.budget_scope: matched optimization steps, not matched wall-clock training cost

analysis.screen: per-cell and per-dataset validation Macro-F1 for Full-S1, 2x2 and 4x1 before training
analysis.recovery: paired 2x2-minus-4x1 best validation MacroDomainF1, per-dataset deltas, learning curves, and separately final-epoch validation results
analysis.aggregation: all nine cells retained; equal-domain means; report mean, median, sample SD and win/tie/loss descriptively

test_policy.metadata_only: The full frozen manifest is parsed to enforce split exclusion; TEST signal data are never loaded.
test_policy.interpretation: Exploratory follow-up designed after publication TEST results were known; validation comparison cannot establish fresh held-out generalization.

runtime_benchmark: Not included in this first runner; equal parameter and recurrent-work budgets do not imply equal latency. Measure both students on identical validation inputs before claiming a superior performance-cost trade-off.
